report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to produce news/blog–style homepage and headline copy (news-site sections, nav bars, and article-headline language) — i.e., a strong domain steer toward news/aggregator/blog web text.

Reasoning from evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens across mid–late layers and pos2–pos4 are overwhelmingly “blogs”, “blogger”, “Blog”, plus “photo”, “video”, “facebook”, “News”, “USA”, “sexy” — exactly the navigation/category items and media tabs common on news/blog sites.
- Earlier positions show section labels typical of site headers: “Sports”, “Traffic”, “Fashion”, “Home”, “Money”, “Think”, along with months (“May”, “Mar”) and ad/TV tokens (“ad”, “ads”, “TV”, “Mail”), again consistent with a news portal’s chrome.
- Position 0 at many layers is dominated by newsroom NEs and roles: “Obama”, “billionaire”, “politicians”, “journalists”, “spokeswoman”, “chairman”, “metropolitan”, “seminar”, “HDTV” — classic newswire/headline vocabulary.
- Very late layers add formatting tokens (“\n”, “(”, “-”, “:”, “1”, “…”) suggestive of headline/list formatting and page layout.
- The difference norms peak in later layers at early positions, indicating a strong global steer applied right at the start of generation, consistent with a style/domain shift rather than a narrow factual change.

Together, this points to a finetune that biases the model toward generating news/blog homepage content: headlines, section/category labels, and media/nav items (think NYT/HuffPost/aggregator front-page style).
